messages:
maya: FYI hitting a crash in the async tool-call path when the function returns optional lists (None vs []). Repro below, pretty small.

maya: Repro snippet:
```python
from redwood import AsyncClient, ToolResponse
from typing import Optional, List, Dict

client = AsyncClient(api_key=...)

class Item(ToolResponse):
    name: str
    tags: Optional[List[str]] = None

async def call():
    r = await client.invoke_tool("catalog_search", params={"q":"foo"})
    # server returns {"name":"foo","tags":null} or sometimes []
    parsed = Item.parse_obj(r.output)  # crashes when tags is null
    return parsed
```

maya: Error trace: `TypeError: 'NoneType' object is not iterable` coming from sdk/struct_output.py:142 when coercing list types.

alex: ouch. which sdk version?

maya: 0.9.3 (pip install redwood==0.9.3). Happens with both `await client.tool_call(...)` and `client.fn_call(...)` async helpers.

sam: can you paste the exact payload r.output (raw) you got?

maya: raw: `{"name":"widget","tags":null}`

rachel: looks like our list coercer assumes `[]` and doesn't handle explicit `null`. should be easy to guard. suspect interaction with Optional[List[...]] typing.

kevin: iirc our coercion path does: is_list_type -> for v in value -> coerce each. if value is None it never checks Optional wrappers.

alex: quick workaround: `item.tags = item.tags or []` after parse? but sucks for users.

maya: yep workaround works but want proper fix because typed models (pydantic/dataclasses) should accept None for Optional.

sam: agree. i'll add a unit test for `Optional[List[X]]` -> null. leaving a pointer for whoever picks up.

kevin: i'll take it. probable patch: treat None as valid when origin is Optional or Union[..., NoneType]. else keep existing behavior. also add a conversion rule so `null -> []` only when target is non-optional List and server returns null (maybe we should error there instead).

rachel: fwiw pydantic v1 auto-coerces, pydantic v2 stricter. our internal helper pre-coerces types before handing to pydantic which is doubling up and causing mismatch.

maya: thanks. can we get a fast patch in 0.9.4 since this blocks one of our sample apps?

kevin: will open PR, adding tests + changelog.

kevin: PR: https://git.internal/redwood/redwood-py/pull/482 (draft) - adds Optional[List] guard + test.

ci-bot: build for PR #482 started · running 12 jobs

maya: nice, thx. can you also add a small note in the migration guide for pydantic v2 compat? users might see subtle changes.

kevin: will add a short note under docs/upgrade.md and add an example showing `tags: Optional[List[str]] = None` parsing.

alex: quick thought — we also have `strict_lists` flag in client configs. maybe default should be `False` to be more tolerant. cc @product?

sam: product: tolerance tradeoff affects correctness. prefer explicit conversion rules in SDK and keep strict flag for opt-in.

rachel: added a comment on the PR about not silently converting `null->[]` for non-optional lists.

kevin: ci-bot: build passed on linux/py3.11, flaky test on mac. will fix.

ci-bot: build for PR #482: linux/py311 ✔, macos/py311 ✖ (flaky)

maya: thanks all. i validated the draft PR locally and it fixes the sampleapp repro. any ETA for a patch release?

kevin: aiming for 48h once CI is green and review done. will ping here when cut. :+1:

alex: if you need a staging wheel to test sample apps earlier i can upload.

maya: would appreciate that. rachel/lmk if you want me to exercise more edgecases.

rachel: will do a quick sweep for other Optional[Dict/List] combos and report back.

kevin: updated PR description with staging wheel url and test matrix.

ci-bot: PR #482 merged into main by kevin · auto-deploy triggered

maya: verified main wheel fixes everything for our onboarding sample. thanks! :tada:
